abstract: Protection and control (P&C) systems are critical to the operation of electricity transmission and distribution networks. The digitisation of the P&C systems has unlocked many new efficiencies and capabilities but has also brought with it new risks with respect to cyber security. The critical role these devices play in interfacing between the ‘cyber world’ and the ‘physical world’ makes them a target for threats for those who want to cause the greatest interruptions to a nation's electricity supplies. A cyber risk methodology using event trees is proposed to understand the benefits of different cyber security controls within existing substation environments. This moves the industry from a maturity driven and checklist based approach towards a risk driven one based on an understanding of cyber security threats; and allowing organisations to produce a cost benefit assessment which may support planned investment as well as providing a justified position when deciding not to invest in particular areas.

articleTitle: Single-ended traveling wave based fault location for single-phase-to-ground in power distribution lines
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Accurately identifying the traveling wave reflected by the fault point is the key to single-ended traveling wave based fault location. Affected by the complex structure and branch lines of the power distribution line, the identification of the traveling waves reflected by the fault point is very difficult. This paper proposes a single-ended fault location for single-phase-to-ground in power distribution lines using switches reclosure generated travelling waves. The paper analyses the difference of travelling waves in three independent line-mode networks and constructs the travelling wave reflected by the fault point directly. And the distance to the fault point from the measuring point is calculated according to the time of switch reclosure generated initial wave and the reflected wave by the fault point. This method is not affected by branch lines and transition resistance. PSCAD simulations verify the accuracy and reliability of the method.

articleTitle: Experimental evaluation of cross-differential protection applied to series-compensated double-circuit lines
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This paper deals with the analysis of cross-differential protection applied to series-compensated double-circuit lines. To evaluate the protection function, it was implemented in a commercially available relay and tested using a real system modelled in Alternative Transients Program (ATP). Due to series compensation, the protection function can lose instantaneous coverage as a result of the subsynchronous resonance and the healthy circuit fault contribution. To prevent incorrect operation, a timed function blocking is needed, which compromises the successive operating mode. However, as a one-terminal based function, the cross-differential protection can still provide a secure operation and be used to enhance the protection scheme for such lines. As the fault is typically detected at least by one terminal, it can also cover all line length using direct transfer trips (DTTs).

articleTitle: CT saturation — A simulation study of different detection and blocking algorithms
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: When one or more terminal current transformers (CTs) become saturated during a through fault, significant spurious differential current can be produced which may cause mal-operation of low impedance differential relays if unmanaged. Encouraging progress has been made in the non-conventional current transformers (CT) technologies such as those based on Rogowski coil or optical sensors. However, until they are fully industrialised and more widely adopted, the onus is on protection relays to counter the impact of CT saturation. The risk is further elevated for busbar protection which experiences a high proportion of through faults and which may see very high current on the faulted feeder due to high concentration of fault MVA. Over the decades, busbar protection products based on different relay technologies ranging from static relays to numerical relays have been in service. The paper describes the effort to model different CT saturation detection and blocking algorithms in the Simulink environment which are then integrated with a bias differential model. Their performances are evaluated by applying COMTRADE test cases that cover a wide range of internal fault, external fault and evolving fault scenarios with varying influencing factors. The test results are analysed with some interesting conclusions drawn.

articleTitle: Experimental evaluation of the alternative generalized alpha plane for double-circuit series-compensated transmission lines
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental evaluation of an alternative generalized alpha plane formulation applied to series compensated double circuit transmission line differential protection. This line configuration introduces major challenges to the protection system, due to the proximity between circuits, in addition to the series compensation effects. Faced with these challenges, the performance of line differential protection allied to the generalized alpha plane strategy is evaluated in a commercial relay. Aiming to do so, various faults scenarios were simulated in a 500 kV series compensated double-circuit, modelled on Alternative Transients Program (ATP). Furthermore, the alternative formulation was directly implemented in the relay and its performance was roughly compared with the original proposal. The obtained results reveal an enhanced performance for the phase elements in comparison with the original method, besides having a more well-behaved response in the alpha plane and a simpler formulation.

articleTitle: Using real-time testing tools to baseline the performance of OT networks for high-speed communications
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the various operational technology (OT) tools available for the performance analysis of mission-critical Ethernet-based communications networks. We describe techniques for simple test cases that provide performance quantification of the communications path in terms of determinism, latency, and availability, using as an example tests performed at the Enel Smart Grid Lab (created by E-Distribuzione in Milan) that were conducted to verify the performance of existing Ethernet network technology when exchanging mission-critical information. Due to similar terminology and comparably appearing networks, many end users use software-based information technology (IT) tools to baseline the performance of OT networks. However, OT networks have different design and performance requirements and require specific, real-time OT tools to verify design implementation and performance. Moreover, an important aspect of testing OT networks is verifying cybersecurity, because the security of the network is directly related to its availability and reliability. A nonsecure network cannot be considered for mission-critical applications, as seen by the repercussions of recent cyberattacks on power systems.

articleTitle: CT sizing for generator and transformer protective relays
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Modern relays often have algorithms that enhance the security of elements that are otherwise susceptible to current transformer (CT) saturation. In this paper, we consider some of the similarities and differences between IEEE and IEC guidance on CT selection. We use CT models verified using high-current tests on a physical CT. Then using these models, we determine CT sizing guidelines and relay settings for a generator and transformer differential relay. Application guidance for generator black start is provided. Considerations such as remanence are discussed.

articleTitle: Parametric sensitivity analysis of actual transmission line time-domain protection relay
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This paper presents a parametric sensitivity analysis of an actual high-speed time-domain line protection relay with the aim to clarify operation aspects which are still scarcely addressed in the literature. A total of 324 faults scenarios on a 500 kV/60 Hz test power system were simulated using the Alternative Transients Program (ATP), which were obtained by varying fault and system features, such as: fault resistance, inception angle, location, type and system loading. The time-domain relay performance was analysed in each scenario, and then, its operation times' probability distribution functions were obtained as a function of the fault distance. The obtained results provide an overall perception on the relay performance regarding its operation times, and point out important practical aspects that can result in additional tripping delays.

articleTitle: Resilient 5G technologies optimized for power grid protection solutions using IEC 61850 time-critical communications
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This paper reports part of the ongoing work being carried out in the scope of the SliceNet project, a vertical business-driven H2020 project in which 5G technologies and services are being developed with the specific goal of serving a heterogeneous set of vertical applications. Efacec and Altice Labs are contributing with a vertical business use case focused on communication-based protection and automation solutions for medium voltage (MV) energy distribution networks. The use case includes the implementation and testing of several distributed algorithms, including high-speed selective blocking using IEC 61850 Routable-Generic Object Oriented Substation Events (R-GOOSE), high-speed post-fault service restoration using R-GOOSE, and differential protection using Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) data transmitted over R-GOOSE. The paper reports on the first stage of lab-based trials that are currently being carried out in the use case testbed, consisting mainly of R-GOOSE communication resilience and high-speed selective blocking over 5G. A small set of the lab tests aim at providing early results for a future viability assessment of the implementation of a differential protection solution over 5G. The results from phase-one trials will be disclosed and analysed, and the plan for the ensuing use case trial stages will be subsequently presented.

articleTitle: Using software-defined networking to build modern, secure IEC 61850-based substation automation systems
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Substation automation systems (SASs) are an essential part of smart grid systems. They consist of intelligent electronic devices (IEDs) communicating using digital communications protocols over a secure local-area network. Today, SASs can support multiple protection, monitoring, and control applications over the same network, allowing real-time decision making by various devices and fast reactions to ever-changing power system states, within a few milliseconds. Additionally, large amounts of data exchanged by devices in an SAS enable smart decision making by stakeholders and improve overall system performance and efficiency. To ensure reliable operation of SASs, a highly secure and resilient communications network backbone is a must. Traditional Ethernet technology was not designed to meet the performance and reliability requirements that are essential for SASs. Moreover, an electric power system is an attractive target for cyber attacks, so modern operational technology (OT) Ethernet networks must be designed with security in mind to protect against cyber threats. In this paper, we discuss an application of software-defined networking (SDN) to meet stringent network performance and cybersecurity requirements. We compare this application to traditional spanning-tree-based networks to show SDN's ability to meet and exceed those requirements.

articleTitle: Multi-vendor interoperability tests of IEDs for HVDC grid protection
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Future large scale HVDC systems will have components from different manufacturers, however, this will require multivendor interoperability. This paper studies multi-vendor interoperability of HVDC protection IEDs using hardware IED prototypes developed by industrial and academic partners. Multi-vendor interoperability tests are performed using real-time hardware-in-the-loop simulations based on open-access converter models configured to represent the proposed three-terminal design of an extension to an existing point-to-point HVDC system in the UK. In particular, this paper focuses on developing testing procedures for IEDs in a multi-vendor environment and identifying possible interoperability issues. Interoperability of two hardware IEDs is demonstrated during primary protection, IED failure backup protection and breaker failure backup protection. In each case, the protection scheme operates correctly and it is shown that, in the studied scenarios, the protection IEDs are interoperable.

articleTitle: Current restrained undervoltage protection scheme of converter dominated microgrids
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This paper presents a current restrained undervoltage protection method for converter dominated microgrids. Current magnitude based conventional protection fails to detect a fault in converter dominated microgrid due to current limiting capability of converters. Fault detection becomes more complicated during islanded operation of such a microgrid. This is because, the current does not exceed the rated value and remains below pickup setting of overcurrent relay during the fault. One alternative is to use undervoltage relay. However, this may not function correctly in the case of a fault at the end of a long cable or a high impedance fault. The current restrained undervoltage based proposed method does not rely on communication and the selectivity can be achieved by using a blinder in a VI-plane. Subsequently, the operating time of the relay is calculated using the index obtained from change in current and voltage inside the blinder. The performance of the proposed method is tested at different fault types and locations with different fault resistance in a converter dominated microgrid.

articleTitle: Impact of synchronous condensers on transmission line protection in scenarios with high penetration of renewable energy sources
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The objective of the studies presented in this paper aims to demonstrate that the deployment and operational control of synchronous condensers in the GB transmission system can mitigate a part of the challenges associated with the high penetration of renewable energy sources. These include the decline of short circuit level and the subsequent impact on transmission line protection schemes. The case studies include scenarios such as transmission-level faults, fault level calculation and assessment of distance protection performance. The results and observations included in the paper aim to highlight the means and supporting evidence for the benefits of synchronous condensers in the view of a fully de-carbonised power system.

articleTitle: Demonstration of partially selective HVDC grid protection system with hardware-in-the-loop IEDs
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This paper aims to demonstrate a partially selective protection strategy for multiterminal VSC-HVDC systems using a simulated industrial case study network. In order to increase confidence that such a protection strategy would be suitable for implementation on a future network, this paper uses hardware protection intelligent electronic devices (IED) prototypes from industry and academia, HVDC circuit breaker models that have been developed in collaboration with manufacturers, and a realistic case study network. The tests performed within this study are used to evaluate the performance of the protection IED in a realistic system, and examine the operation of the partially selective protection strategy at the system level. Results presented indicate that each IED achieved fast fault detection, reliable discrimination, and that the circuit breaker models were able to successfully isolate the faulted circuit, indicating the success of the partially selective protection strategy.

articleTitle: Operational testing of virtual and physical IEDs using GOOSE for protection application
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The integration of Operation Technology such as Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs) brings added challenges for testing and operation of complex interconnected protection systems. The hardware limitations of IEDs, such as integration in existing infrastructure and reduced run time control, limits engineers and researchers to test complex protection and automation scenarios. Virtualization of these technologies, allows seamless integration of software units into existing systems, which can be scaled up for large scale system testing. In this paper, the operation of virtual IEDs has been validated with that of physical IEDs. Two separate test platforms are used; one for the physical IED infrastructure and the other for virtual IED (vIED) infrastructure. A use case for overcurrent feeder protection using GOOSE communication has been demonstrated. The performance of circuit breaker tripping and GOOSE communication has been demonstrated and compared for both the test platforms. The vIED operational ability is validated and key insights for future work are given.

articleTitle: Requirements for open specifications in multi-vendor HVDC protection systems
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Integrating multiterminal high-voltage direct-current (HVDC) connections into the existing alternating current (AC) power transmission system is a possible solution for transport of large amounts of renewable energy. Protection is considered a key enabler for multiterminal HVDC (MTDC) grids. Designing such a protection system is a challenge, in particular in a multivendor setup. Fault detection during transients might be required to achieve the stringent speed requirements for HVDC protection. This in turn requires knowledge about the expected system behaviour during faults and involves knowledge from all vendors supplying equipment in MTDC grid. Traditionally, HVDC projects are, however, supplied as turn-key solutions and the control and protection systems are the intellectual property of the vendors and not open for the HVDC endusers. This paper aims to provide a starting point on the discussion which information has to be shared between vendors and HVDC end-users when designing MTDC grid protection. Simulations results show that missing information about certain aspects can lead to a failure of the protection system. A discussion on organization of the available information is added. Open specifications of the used equipment are useful to design safe and reliable MTDC grid protection.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of phasor measurement units with sampled value input
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Synchrophasors produced by phasor measurement units (PMUs) are widely used in modern power systems for wide-area monitoring, protection and control applications. Contemporary technology allows a PMU to acquire its instantaneous voltage and current inputs digitally from sampled values (SV). This work investigates the electrical performance of two commercial PMUs with SV input in accordance with prevailing IEC/IEEE standards. The paper also presents a performance comparison of PMUs with SV input against ones with conventional hardwired analogue input. A digital real-time simulator is used to generate theoretical test signals and publish SV (as per IEC 61869-9) into PMUs under test. Both steady-state and dynamic performance of PMUs are evaluated using a test automation and analysis tool. It is evident from the results obtained that PMUs with SV input, when correctly interfaced, produce robust and accurate measurements.

articleTitle: Greenstart: Protection challenges with integrating wind power parks into system restoration
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Many power grids are experiencing very high penetrations of inverter-interfaced energy sources such as wind power parks, solar power parks, and battery energy storage systems. Most system restoration plans incorporate such resources very late or at the very end of the restoration process. Should a blackout occur during a period with a high penetration of such resources, however, many conventional thermal generators could be offline and cold. In such a scenario the load restoration time could be delayed by several hours as the time for these generators to reach rated output is limited by their maximum heat-rate. This paper will investigate the protection challenges to integrating inverter-interfaced energy sources early into system restoration.

articleTitle: Frequency domain analysis of HVDC grid non-unit protection
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Owing to the fact that the propagated travelling waves following a DC fault in HVDC grids consist of a wide range of frequencies, frequency domain analysis provides a useful means to assess DC protection schemes, including non-unit protection schemes. Non-unit protection uses series inductors at key nodes to distinguish between internal and external faults, exploiting the fact that these inductors present high impedance at high frequencies. Consequently the transient voltage frequency response in each fault case is recognisably different. On this basis, the investigation in the frequency domain can reveal significant information for protection design purposes. Towards this aim, the transient voltage at the relay location is meticulously represented in the frequency domain by taking into account the transmission medium length and geometry, the number of other attached feeders to the same bus, the converter parameters, the inductive termination, the fault resistance, and the travelling wave behaviour of DC faults. By performing a sensitivity analysis on these parameters, a deeper understanding of their impact on HVDC non-unit protection is obtained. In addition, the factors that can be adjusted to extend the reach of the protection systems are revealed and a generic approach for analytically calculating the protection threshold is developed.

articleTitle: Compliance of a cable-based protection strategy for OHL grids: Analysis and remediation
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This paper points out the challenges to overcome when applying a protection strategy based on a non-selective fault clearing philosophy without DC reactors to an overhead line based multi-terminal DC grid. One of the main problems to overcome is the development of a reliable protection algorithm, which is able to discriminate both, the faulty pole and the faulty line. After a theoretical part on the initial voltage surge in phase and modal domains, a wave-front based algorithm is proposed and tested in a Multi-Terminal DC grid using Electro-Magnetic Transient software EMTP-RV. In the last section, component specifications for DC circuit breakers in OHL based DC grids are provided. Key performance indicators are applied in order to compare the performances of both conductor types while using the same protection strategy.

articleTitle: Influence of collection network parameters on performance of distance protection directional elements in offshore wind farms
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Distance protection is one of the most advanced protection functions and is widely used in big-scale offshore wind farms (OWFs) as a main protection of collection array cables of different voltage levels. However, practical experience shows that performance of distance protection can be affected by various operational and design parameters of OWFs collection networks. The paper evaluates the influence of these parameters on response of distance protection directional elements of different types during single line to ground faults. Analysis has been performed using DIgSILENT PowerFactory software and the results have been verified by testing of several commercial distance protection relays in a laboratory environment. The paper reveals that the performance of some of the investigated distance protection directional elements can be severely affected by combinations of different system parameters of OWFs collection networks whereas some directional elements are stable. Several strategies to limit the negative effect of influencing system parameters are proposed.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity based on IEC 62351 and IEC 62443 for IEC 61850 systems
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The word “cyber,” originating from the Greek word meaning “skilled steering or guidance,” has taken on the modern meaning of using digital communications within and among intelligent devices to perform information gathering and commanded control. Information technology (IT) systems include networked communications among computers, business systems, and the internet. Operational technology (OT) systems include networked communications among industrial control system (ICS) devices performing automatic safety, operational, and monitoring processes. In this paper, established ICS methods and standards are used to design defense-in-depth cybersecurity methods for digital communications within an energy control system (ECS) communications network. The ECS communications architecture is a mission-critical ICS and is divided into multiple levels with unique requirements and features from the process up through the station and finally to the control center. Using these levels, it is possible to identify interacting cyber defense technologies, the levels at which they should be deployed, and which devices they belong to (IEC 62443 Part 3) instead of the arbitrary defense-in-breadth strategy of requesting that every device include every cyber defense technology (IEC 62443 Part 4).

articleTitle: Experiences in dynamic line rating (DLR) using a wireless line monitoring system (ILMS)
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: More renewable resources require increased power system capacity. As there are financial restrictions or government regulations making it difficult to build new transmission lines to reinforce the network. The Wireless Monitoring System of Distribution Lines is based on sensors that are installed directly in the distribution lines. Complemented with wheatear station, in turn send the measurement information (phasor current, conductor temperature, wind speed and direction) to a hub (usually installed on the MV pole). By using advanced analysis tools, additional intelligence in the power distribution network is provided to improve the reliability and efficiency of the network by using a web server-side software to dynamically calculate the line rating. and provides a configuration mechanism for the console to allow mapping of the algorithm inputs to the measurements available in the system. This approach allows using the same calculation mechanism for line sag, or DLR algorithms. Paper describes experiences with data obtained from the field, showing increases of energy transfer of around 11% up to 160% of the line nominal power. This brings an economic benefit for users to maximize the use of their assets, matching the operation with the generation characteristics of intermittent generation sources such as wind and solar.

articleTitle: DC offset removal for phase estimation based on DNN in power system using less than one cycle waveform
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The amount of electrical consumption rises gradually every year which puts an enormous strain on electrical power systems and electrical protective systems. Dealing with this issue, automatic protective systems have been developed relentlessly; however, DC-offset in fault current is still the main issue to solve since it makes many protective devices operate inaccurately which lead to both unreliable and unsecured power systems. Modifying Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) in phasor domain is quite well known for solving DC-offset, however the drawback of this method is that more than one cycle waveform is essential to complete the task. This paper proposed Deep Neural Network method to estimate fault current phase angle using only 90.625% of a cycle waveform during DC Offset phenomenon. With enough intensive DNN training, the DNN algorithm manage to show an accurate result while using less input signal which could cut down the operating time. Not only DC-offset signal, but the results show that DNN is also robust against DC-offset with noise and harmonics.

articleTitle: Study on coordination of protective relays in distribution system with distributed generation
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: In the recent decade, many countries around the globe have been increased the proportion of electrical power generation from renewable energy sources, which results in rising in the penetration level of distributed generation (DG). However, the installation of DG into the distribution system may raise many issues that can impact the distribution system in both the technical and economic aspects. When DG is connected to a distribution system, it can affect the performance of the system and the protective device already installed owing to the change of voltage level, short-circuit level and direction of power flow in the system. For this reason, a protective device may cause the malfunction because the bus impedance of the system is changed; this will result in a change of the current in each bus. This paper aims to study the coordination between the protective relay and the DG installed into the distribution system. The distribution system under investigation is a part of the Provincial Electricity Authority (PEA). Under this research, DG data that are connected to the PEA distribution is used. The simulations are performed using digital simulation and electrical network calculation program (DIgSILENT).

articleTitle: Challenges for earth-fault protections due to extensive use of cables in the grid
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Capacitive zero-sequence currents do exist in any power system during an earth-fault regardless network grounding principles. However, existence of these currents is typically ignored in traditional protection practice. In many countries some type of high-impedance grounding is used which limits the earth-fault current to a certain level. Increased use of cables in medium voltage distribution grids and high voltage sub-transmission grids can also significantly raise the capacitive earth fault currents, which in combination with the used grounding principle in the power network can pose a problem for proper operation of some relays.

articleTitle: Ease commissioning of a line differential scheme by sharing an Ethernet-based protection interface
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Line differential protection system operators are always challenged with providing the required communications channel, i.e. the protection data interface, between the remote ends of the protection system, where the relays are installed. Nowadays most substations are equipped with network access. Leveraging such standard Ethernet-based communication for line differential protection enables for cost-effective installations. Additionally, during commissioning of line differential schemes, the protection engineers are challenged with setup and test of distributed devices in remote substations. Relays which can reuse and share a single Ethernet-based communication for relay setup, can be accessed and parameterized from a single PC connected to the protection system at one end only. The same communication channel can be reused for protection testing too. This simplifies end-to-end testing considerably, if a test system is used, which can control multiple distributed test sets for injection of voltage and current test signals from a single software on one end of the scheme. The proposed concept will ease commissioning of line differential protection systems in areas with limited reception of GPS and mobile data communication, e.g. in a tunnel or in a cavern.

articleTitle: The role of regulation in ensuring effective power system protection
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This paper summarises steps taken by the Omani electricity sector to bring protection to a level necessary to enable the power sector to deliver benefits expected to customers. This included a comprehensive review of codes, standards, policies, training and resources available with respect to power system protection. Since restructuring in 2005, the electricity sector in Oman invested to meet rapidly increasing demand for electricity. For around 10 years there was double digit growth in customer numbers and peak demand, which necessitated significant rapid growth in transmission and distribution networks. Companies, contractors, consultants and suppliers were pushed hard to meet project deadlines. The efforts and results were outstanding, but protection related blackouts suggested that there may be a problem, hence a project was initiated. What was found was enlightening. Whilst some standards and the codes needed updating to reflect new systems being brought to the system, the underlying problem was the lack of appreciation of the importance of protection at higher levels of organisations. This left protection engineers in a difficult and unappreciated position. This paper describes the work undertaken to address the problems found, and the success that was achieved.

articleTitle: A centralized protection and control system using a well proven transmission class protection relay
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The growing adoption of process bus digital substation is leading to a new interest in the concept of centralized protection and control, where all protection functions for a substation are combined into a single device. When considering implementations of this solution, it is important to remember that these devices will be installed in substations and must meet all the expected requirements for protective devices in substations. Importantly, they must be a technologically mature solution, using proven protection algorithms, scalable for any substation size, on hardware capable of the expected 20-year service life, while providing all the functionality of a complete protection system. This paper describes one specific actual implementation of such a system for distribution substations, based on an existing transmission class protection relay. This centralized distribution system takes advantages of features already developed for the transmission protection platform, including: - Proven protection algorithms for feeder, bus, and transformer protection - A robust cyber security implementation - Support for multiple SCADA protocols - Support for IEC 61850, including sampled values subscription - Numerous communications ports to support separate connections to station bus, process bus, and engineering networks simultaneously A growing requirement for distribution substations is the ability to integrate into wide area monitoring, protection and control schemes. As the device is based on a transmission-based relay platform, this ability is quickly met by including multiple Phasor Measurement Units, and the use of Routable GOOSE to provide inter-station events and control indications.

articleTitle: Leveraging a service oriented architecture for automatic retrieval and processing of COMTRADE files for analysis needs of maintenance of circuit breakers
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Maintenance of power system components is fundamental to ensure high quality operations and avoid malfunctioning. Given the crucial role of the circuit breakers (CBs) in ensuring quality of power systems operation, this paper presents work on implementation of an automatic retrieval and processing of COMTRADE recordings with the aim to compute quantities relevant for maintenance and preventive maintenance of the CBs. For this purpose, a Service Oriented Architecture (SOA) implemented as an Enterprise Service Bus (ESB) is developed on top of the COMTRADE repository system. This architecture is then connected with two applications able to automatically retrieve, decode and use the recordings of the fault to obtain specific indicators on the health of some parts of the CBs. The approach filters data and utilises the Wavelet Transform analysis to identify anomalies in the COMTRADE recordings. Based on this analysis, it is possible to compute the duration of the fault and assess its impact on CBs. Even if lack of common metadata for fault recordings prevents generalization on the topic and excludes the possibility of applying machine learning techniques, the project shows that the resulting layered architecture composed of power system, SOA and applications, allows to automatically obtain indicators on the state of the CBs' components. Consequently, decision making for maintenance of the circuit breakers is enhanced. Moreover, the flexible nature of the implemented structure, utilising a Service Oriented Architecture, allows for future extensions and improvements applicable also for wider scenarios.

articleTitle: Phasor-based and time-domain transmission line protection considering wind power integration
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The increasing integration of converter-interfaced wind power plants into the existing power systems has been a challenge for protection and monitoring functions. As a result, studies on protection performance considering this type of generation have been a topic of great interest to the industry. In this way, this paper evaluates the performance of phasor-based and time-domain protection functions available in real micro-processed protective devices when applied to a 500 kV/60 Hz transmission line that interconnects a wind power generation plant to a traditional power system. The test system was modelled and simulated by means of the Power System Simulator (PS Simul) software, through which different fault scenarios were evaluated by varying parameters such as fault location, fault resistance and inception angle. The obtained results highlight differences in evaluated protective relays' performances when applied to both line terminals, revealing the impact of converter-interfaced wind power plants on the relays' reliability and operation times.

articleTitle: Design and commissioning of a secure substation network architecture
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Utilities and cyber security auditors are increasingly considering not only the control centre as critical attack vector, but also substations as potential entry points for cyber attacks. Important risk factors are the processes, how the commissioning of the protection and control systems are realized and how remote maintenance access is implemented. Therefore, the architecture of the protection and control system must be reviewed for security. To achieve this, the Swiss generation and distribution utility Centralschweizer Kraftwerke AG (CKW) started a project in 2016/2017 to develop a new reference architecture for their secondary systems. Their design addresses these attack vectors with countermeasures, while still offering a sensible balance between maintainability and security. The design includes multiple levels of security including multiple firewall layers. Additionally, an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is applied. Selecting a suitable IDS for substations proved out to be challenging, as many IDS don't support the requirements of substation networks. This paper starts with an enumeration of the most important attack vectors on substations, followed by a description of the security architecture implemented for the first time in a new greenfield 110kV substation project by CKW. The paper concludes with the experiences in selecting a suitable IDS for substations and the lessons learned in the factory acceptance test of this project.

articleTitle: From substation automation systems to protection. developing an approach for testing of protection, automation and control
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: IEC 61850 became the widely accepted standard communication in protection, automation and control. Test approaches to be used for protection systems communicating via GOOSE and Client/Server communication according to IEC 61850 are available for some time already and well established. Substation Automation Systems with IEC 61850 became more powerful. Taking this into account the demand for testing the automation and control became obvious. The paper describes the testing approach. Security patches demand continuous testing preferred performed automatically. This extension of the approach will be proposed. Protection and Control must be tested together since they are not divided in terms of devices and functionalities in any case. This paper proposes a holistic approach testing the entire chain and interfaces between protection, automation and control. Performing this approach demands high quality in engineering files according to the standard (SCL files, Substation Configuration Language). This paper describes requirements and experiences with existing tools and files. The paper focuses on practical experiences. It explains dependencies between protection and application and explains the use case considering experiences in combines functionalities as auto recloser, synchro check and direct transfer schemes. Interlocking as essential part for security will be covered as well, since the testing is time consuming and challenging. This paper describes automated testing functionalities delivering time savings and increasing the reliability of the protection system. An outlook, considering the application of Sampled Values for protection, automation and control finalizes the paper

articleTitle: National grid application of high impedance busbar zone protection using electromechanical technology. In service testing and maintenance to prolong asset life – a utility experience
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The development of the 400kV supergrid system in England & Wales led to the introduction of rigorous standards for the design and performance of busbar zone protection at 400kV stations. These standards evolved to a refined level to incorporate circuit-breaker fail and back tripping and fully duplicated facilities allowing testing, maintenance, fault investigation and extensions to take place with the protection in service. Although a policy of applying numerical busbar protection was adopted in 2000, National Grid operates many stations which are still equipped with electromechanical busbar zone protection and when regularly maintained these installations have proved to be very reliable. This paper outlines some of the technical challenges in asset stewardship of equipment which is up to seventy years old and explains National Grid's approach to in service testing and maintenance of conventional busbar zone protection.

articleTitle: Formal methods to power-system automation based on Petri Nets
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: In this work, after surveying the current available methods and formats for specification of functional requirements of PAC systems used by the industry and analysing their advantages and disadvantages, a formal method approach based on Petri Nets is proposed to power-system automation.

articleTitle: Use of IEC 61850 for wide area operational tripping schemes to improve stability response
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Remedial action schemes are widely used in transmission networks to maintain system stability, security and overall reliability against contingencies. In the UK transmission network, National Grid utilises a form of remedial action scheme known as Operational Tripping Schemes (OTS) to achieve this, by constraining generation or taking other corrective actions such as the de-loading of an HVDC interconnector. This paper explains the challenges of redesigning an existing OTS which protects the transmission grid of the south-east coast of England, to comply with consequential requirements on the speed of operation caused by the introduction of new interconnection and generation to the network. The paper outlines the design methodology of utilising IEC 61850 GOOSE messaging over wide-area communications infrastructure. In this paper, the state-of-the-art design to manage optimised processing of data, utilising distributed logic algorithms to specify OTS actions to the devices assigned for each controllable generation asset is also presented.

articleTitle: Protection functionality and performance with declining system fault levels and inertia within national grid electricity transmission system in the United Kingdom
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This paper summarizes a study performed by National Grid UK to understand the impact of declining fault levels and system inertia due to increasing penetration of renewable, inverter-based generation. With the proliferation of this power-electronics-based generation, it is no longer possible to ignore the impacts to transmission system characteristics, especially changes in system fault currents and inertia. The focus of this study was to investigate these impacts on transmission system protection and control equipment, as well as to explore possible mitigation strategies to address these impacts. Any mitigation actions to address these issues will be at a significant cost and therefore an in-depth understanding of these issues will be needed by any utility experiencing such phenomena. In addition, power-electronic-based generation has relatively more complex behaviour under power system faults than what is well understood from synchronous generator characteristics. The behaviour in response to a fault is significantly influenced by vendor-specific design of electronic control schemes, as well as the inherent fast-response (inertia-less) characteristics. Hence, the impact on transmission system protection is completely different from that of conventional rotating-machine-based generation.

articleTitle: Testing busbar protection (BBP) systems using process bus technology
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Busbar protection (BBP) is the most complex protection system in a substation, as it interfaces to all bays in the substation. Every required current, disconnector status, and circuit breaker status and control point must be wired into the BBP relay in some manner. As a result, BBP relays are the most difficult and time consuming to test. A conventional centralized busbar protection has complicated wiring, as wiring for all currents, status, and control points must be installed to the main unit. Conventional distributed busbar protection simplifies field wiring by using bay units as the interface point to field wiring. Most use dedicated point-to-point fiber optic connections between the bay units and the central unit, requires requiring a fiber optic cable and communications port at the central unit for each bay. Process bus is distributed I/O for protection and control, converting analog interfaces to digital data at the source, using merging units (MUs) for currents and voltages and switchgear control units (SCUs) for status and control, and process interfaces units (PIUs), MUs and SCUs as one, as interface devices. Integrating process bus in busbar protection keeps field wiring the same as with distributed protection: wiring for each bay is connected to a merging unit. The advantage is that the merging units and the busbar protection unit are connected to the process bus communications network, using IEC 61850-based communications and standard time synchronization. The busbar protection unit needs only a single port or redundant ports with high availability network protocols such as PRP (Parallel Redundancy Protocol) and HSR (High-availability Seamless Redundancy) as defined in IEC 62439-3 [1] to collect all data needed for protection. Boundary clock time synchronization technology can be built in the relay to allow the process bus busbar protection relay to act as a master clock to synchronize all the merging units in the system, extending the process bus busbar protection to be used in both digital substation and conventional substation without requiring GPS clock synchronization. Utilizing the process bus technology in busbar protection simplifies the busbar protection testing also. This paper reviews busbar protection under process bus, along with general concepts in testing process bus protection systems. Specifically, the paper outlines testing strategies for a busbar protection relay that can subscribe to, and use, up to 24 SV data streams, including both commissioning and maintenance testing. Included in these strategies is the proper use of test modes and simulated SV and GOOSE messages. An important learning from these discussions is how testing a bus bar protection relay under IEC 61850-based process bus is simpler, and carries less risk, than testing a conventional busbar protection relay.

articleTitle: Use of IEC 61850 parameters for settings of protection and automation functions
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This paper gives some examples of the use of IEC 61850 based settings and describes the associated requirements for their implementation, import and life-time management. Several issues are discussed in detail, namely the mandatory use of primary values for settings and some identified shortcomings in setting parameters in the current editions of IEC 61850. In addition to settings available as IEC 61850 Data Objects (DO), user settings not defined in IEC 61850 require a mapping to settings defined by the manufacturer. Whilst the aim should be to use native IEC 61850 parameters for all user settings, an approach to map user settings to manufacturer specific parameters in an automated way is described. The paper also discusses the configuration mechanism defined to map DO published by protection functions to subscribing protection related functions depending on the intended use. This distinction needs to be conveyed by the IEC 61850 configuration file. In a more general way, this is one possibility to use the configuration file to indicate which variant of a function needs to be instantiated.

articleTitle: Time domain mapping of energised underground low voltage cable network topologies
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The paper describes the use of Pulse Transit Time (PTT) fault location methods in conjunction with pre-calculated time domain maps of cables. The accuracy of the mapping can be checked by a simple technique whereby a portable Marker unit is applied to the energised cable. In addition, the PTTs produced by permanent faults can be confirmed when they are exposed for repair. The technique described in the paper allows the location of transitory and intermittent faults to be determined with high accuracy and a pro-active approach to supply outage reduction adopted.

articleTitle: Development and test of an adaptive single-pole auto-reclose function
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Most faults in solidly grounded high voltage (HV) networks are transient single-phase arcing faults, primarily cleared by single-pole tripping. Yet in many cases a secondary arc is evolving due to the capacitive and inductive coupling from the healthy line phases. This secondary arc eventually extinguishes after some time and auto-reclosing should be executed only after extinction of this secondary arc, because it will be unsuccessful otherwise. This need forces to set long single-pole dead times. A new adaptive auto-reclose function has been developed, which detects the presence and extinction of a secondary arc by monitoring the level of total harmonic distortion (THD) and voltage amplitude at fundamental frequency of the faulty phase voltage (of course this requires line-side voltage transformers (VTs)). Either no arc is present, or the arc is extinguished, if the THD level is small and the fundamental voltage amplitude is reasonably high. If both criteria are fulfilled, the dead time is adapted by the protection relay accordingly. For testing such adaptive auto-reclose functions a simulation-based test, which models a secondary arc as a non-linear element, has been used. The arc is modelled as a simple two-state non-linear fault, which ignites if a certain voltage threshold is exceeded and extinguishes again at the next current zero-crossing. This will result in substantial THD during active arc and clear fundamental frequency voltage as soon as the fault is disappeared. A lot of test cases were executed to cover all the different possible scenarios and timings of the secondary arc behaviour (with and without successful reclosing). Therefore, an iterative closed-loop approach within the simulation-based test software was used to mimic the real-time behaviour of a hardware-in-the-loop test system and simulate correct reaction upon the trip and close commands of the relay under test. The simulated signals are well in line with recordings from real-world events. Such recordings were initially used to validate the function, too, but don't allow full function assessment. Meanwhile first pilot installations of the new function are set up on transmission systems and first field feedback can be presented.

articleTitle: A novel pilot protection for transmission lines based on full travelling wave signal polarities
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: It is well known that travelling wave protection concepts have certain advantages for transmission line protection applications. The most obvious advantages are the fast fault detection speed, good security in case of series compensated lines, power swings, current transformer saturations. With the progress both in digital signal processing and increased protection speed demand in the power systems, it is time to apply travelling wave protection into modern numerical relays. This paper proposes a newly developed pilot protection solution based on the fault induced travelling wave polarities. Firstly, the operation issues related with the security and dependability on the existing travelling wave protection relays have been analysed. This includes the possible wrong polarity detections due to harmonics or noises in the network, dependability issue in special system conditions. Secondly, the new solution is provided based on the use of full travelling wave signal polarity information with a two terminal line model as an example. In order to further enhance the security, a high-pass filter concept is introduced. Moreover, three polarity solutions both for the weak system condition or strong system condition are proposed to improve dependability. Finally, the total solution is verified based on PSCAD simulation model with conclusion provided.

articleTitle: Interoperability of line differential protection
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Line differential protection is used for a long time to protect overhead lines and cables in transmission and distribution systems. The basic principle of line differential protection is Kirchhoff's current law. Due to this principle line differential protection is strictly selective to clear faults on the protected line. To apply Kirchhoff's current law a line differential protection needs the currents from both ends of the protected line. The currents from the local end can be measured directly by means of current transformers, connected to the line differential protection device. The remote end currents however cannot be measured directly by the local line differential protection device. In general, the remote end currents are measured by a line differential protection device of same type and afterwards sent via communication link. Due to bandwidth restrictions of the communication link, differences in pre-processing of the measured values and other device specific implementations there is no interoperability of line differential protection. In general line differential protection requires both devices to be from the same manufacturer. Often the same device type or even the same firmware version is required. Today there is no interoperability for line differential protection. In case one substation gets an update of the line differential protection, the remote substation needs an update of the related line differential protection too. This paper describes an actual case how interoperability was achieved for line differential protection of different protection platforms of one manufacturer. The problems and limitations for this use case are explained in detail. In addition to this the paper suggests an implementation of line differential protection based on sampled measured values and GOOSE according to IEC61850 and IEC61869. With this approach, the communication interface between the line differential protection devices becomes interoperable. More flexible solutions are found to be possible. For instance, a line differential scheme might consist of only one line differential relay, receiving sampled measured values from a merging unit located at the remote end. The trip command for the remote end might be transferred back via GOOSE to the merging unit located at the remote end. For redundancy even two different line differential protection relays could be used feeding each other with the sampled measured values from the remote end.

articleTitle: Impact of converter-based distributed generation units on fault behaviour of distribution grids
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This research investigates the impact of converter-based generation on the fault behaviour of distribution grids. For this, two control system designs for grid-following and grid-forming converters are presented. These control designs are implemented in transient simulation models. By considering a phase-to-phase asymmetrical fault in two specific grid topologies, the impact of injecting negative sequence fault current on the short-circuit levels and its consequences for overcurrent protection is investigated. The results suggest that, in the presented scenarios, injecting negative sequence currents leads to a minor increase of fault currents. Yet, due to the stringent current limitations, the fault current contribution of converters remains limited, regardless what type of control system is used.

articleTitle: Interoperability among DC protection strategies based on fault blocking converters and DC circuit breakers within a multi-terminal HVDC system
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Multi-terminal HVDC grids based on Modular Multilevel Converters (MMCs) are considered a promising solution for the large-scale integration of renewable energy sources into existing transmission systems. Depending on the AC network constraints, the DC grids' extension and available breaker technologies, different protection schemes can be suitable for DC line fault clearing. Due to the absence of standards for HVDC systems, several of these protection strategies are already in place and might be present within an envisioned meshed DC grid. The functional interoperability among different protection schemes and converter technologies is investigated in this paper, focussing on strategies based on DC circuit breakers (DCCBs) and strategies based on fault blocking converters (FBCs) in combination with high-speed switches (HSS). Analyses are carried out on a four-terminal, symmetric monopolar cabled system using simulations in PSCAD|EMTDC™. The results show that the combination of the two approaches needs adaption to allow fault clearing without a deterioration of both the system stresses and the recovery after a fault. A fully selective approach adapting the breaker capabilities at each line, as well as protection adaptions towards a partially selective approach splitting the grid into fully and non-selective protection zones are presented.

articleTitle: Testing of protection in a digital substation protection automation and control system (SPACS)
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This paper will be based on the work of CIGRE WG B5.53 [1] and it will cover the testing of the complete digital functional chain, including the use of process bus for the transmission of the analogue values and station bus for the transmission of trip orders and other signals for substation protection, automation and control systems (SPACS). The focus will be on testing of protection in a fully digital IEC 61850 [2] substations and equipment. The increasing levels of functional integration result in the development of many multifunctional Intelligent Electronic Device (IEDs) that require interfaces with multiple primary devices. Testing of SPACS at its most basic is the creation of simulated inputs to a function or device to verify the operation and performance expectations taking into account the type of test and the traffic on the communication network. When testing a fully digital substation, it is necessary to create simulated data as inputs to specific Logical Nodes (LN) or Logical Devices (LD). In order to publish simulated data for testing, it is necessary to use a data message which the SPACS communication network can accept and transmit.

articleTitle: Machine learning based anomaly-based intrusion detection system in a full digital substation
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The cyberattacks that occurred in recent years have raised concerns in critical infrastructures, including power system networks. Identifying ongoing attacks is essential to enable the energy industry to respond to adversaries. Many commercial products and research projects include machine learning based intrusion detection systems but there is still a need for understanding the data training requirements for those systems in order to successfully deploy them to protect power systems. This paper presents the development of an anomaly-based Intrusion Detection System (IDS) based on a machine learning methodology to create a whitelist. The system was implemented using GNU Octave. It was trained using traffic flow from real devices generated from a Virtual Site Acceptance Testing and Training (VSATT) platform where multi-vendor secondary devices were set up and communicated to each other. The system was then tested using different datasets which were also generated from the VSATT platform. Results show that the implemented IDS performed correctly under different case studies. The results also indicate that the learned traffic identifies GOOSE and MMS messages based on the normal behaviours from those protocols, but the presence of other messages might require manual inputs to be incorporated in the training dataset.

articleTitle: Identification of faulty conductors in HVdc links connecting future offshore wind sites
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: In this paper, a method to identify the fault type and the conductors involved in a fault is demonstrated for a complex HVdc transmission configuration advantageous for interconnection of future offshore windfarms with onshore AC grids. A number of bipole voltage source converter (VSC) based offshore rectifier stations connected through two-conductor submarine cables to a three-conductor overhead transmission line which is connected to a line commutated converter (LCC) based inverter station is considered. Fault types are identified by comparing the maximum rates of change of locally measured currents. With the help of detailed simulations, the capability of identifying the pole(s) involved in a fault in an about 1ms is demonstrated. Furthermore, it is verified that the method is not adversely affected by the fault resistance or the location of application, i.e. the onshore LCC inverter or the offshore VSC rectifiers.

articleTitle: Standardisation of high impedance protection schemes
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: High impedance impedance protection is a well-established protection principle used in many applications. Whilst calculations are straightforward, especially for new schemes, they are often done on a per-scheme basis despite commonalities across projects and applications. This is due to variations in system earthing, switchgear rating, current transformers, relay types and application. Ad-hoc calculation of settings can lead to highly variable settings and resistor specifications. Retrofitting of resistors in protection panels during commissioning can lead to additional cost and delays on projects. UKPN have therefore undertaken analysis of worst case conditions and sensitivity analysis to define standard settings, resistors and non-linear resistors. Resistors and non-linear resistors can be confirmed early in the design process to avoid delays during commissioning. The standard settings, resistors and non-linear resistors work for a wide variety of cases and are cheaper than custom resistors if engineering cost and project programme risk are considered.

articleTitle: A new digital distance element implementation using coincidence timing
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This paper presents a new distance protection element implementation that is based on the classic analogue principle of coincidence timing between the distance element operating and polarizing signals. The paper explains the basics of coincidence timing and the many advantages of this approach. It explains why early digital relays could not afford this implementation method and why they settled on using heavily-filtered phasors. The paper focuses on describing a modern digital implementation of distance protection elements based on coincidence timing that combine advantages of the core analogue principle with several extensions and improvements taking advantage of the digital relay technology. The new algorithm has been implemented in a hardware platform and consistently operates with speed on the order of half a cycle. The paper illustrates the new approach using a field case and shows laboratory test results from hardware-in-the-loop tests.

articleTitle: Case study: Adaptive load shedding in critical industrial facilities
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Industrial plant activities involve critical processes, especially those that include the use of toxic gases. In the event of a loss of electricity supply, such processes can fail and cause lethal health risks to those near the plants. In industrial plants that rely on their own power generation and are interconnected to an electric utility for energy backup, both the power system topology and the importance and criticality of the electrical loads across these plants change dynamically as processes and operations are initiated or stopped. In the event of a fault, an effective load-shedding scheme that adapts automatically to changes in system topology, such as islanded and non-islanded conditions, is key to compensate for lost generation, maintain power system stability, and avoid blackouts. This paper describes the design, implementation, and operational results of an in-service load-shedding scheme for a large chemical industrial complex in Mexico. The proposed load-shedding scheme uses high-speed IEC 61850 Generic Object-Oriented Substation Event (GOOSE) messages and synchrophasors, which provide apparatus monitoring and control, remote load shedding, and monitoring of power measurements for onsite generators and the interconnection with the electric utility system.

articleTitle: The behaviour of virtual synchronous machine (VSM) based converters in front of non-saturable faults
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Power converter penetration has increased substantially in the last 20 years bringing new challenges from the system protection perspective. The power network is undergoing a major transformation as the major part of new installed power comes from non-synchronous sources such as wind or solar. These changes might lead to malfunction of the conventional protection schemes such as overcurrent protection or distance protection relays. At the same time, the reduction of the system inertia might cause the tripping of the Loss of Main protection due to a very aggressive Rate of Change of Frequency. To enhance the grid voltage source characteristic and mitigate the loss of inertia, a new set of converter controllers known as Grid forming Converter or Virtual Synchronous Machine has been suggested in recent years. The performance of VSM could provide a potential advantage compared to traditional power converter controllers when a large frequency deviation occurs helping to keep the system stable. This article quantifies and compares the performance of different converter control algorithms including Current Vector Control, Virtual Synchronous Machine and Power Synchronisation Control in front of different frequency events.

articleTitle: Process bus for bus differential — Challenges, solutions, and opportunities
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The use of process bus and Non-Conventional Instrument Transformers (NCIT) are a logical step in improved bus protection. Different bus protection principles will see different levels of process bus penetration. High impedance bus differential protection may still be used in many applications however this principle will not be impacted by process bus technology due to the operating characteristics. All types of low impedance bus differential protection will benefit from process bus technology. The paper discusses how the use of merging units will close the gap between centralized busbar protection and distributed busbar protection. The concept of merging unit as a function instead of a physical device enables numerous different solutions. A merging unit can be designed as a plain device; only feeding the bus differential protection with sampled measured values, or it can be implemented with a feeder or line protection relay where the main function is to protect the incoming or outgoing line or feeder as well as delivering the sampled measured value to the busbar protection. This concept is used to save in device count, wiring and engineering work. Process bus technology enables the possibility to use NCIT. This technology has great advantages such as higher accuracy and fewer problems with CT-saturation. There are also constraints which should be considered, and these are discussed. Based on the transient requirements given in related standards, recommendations are given for the use of NCIT for bus differential protection. Different communication topologies for bus differential protection are reviewed and checked against the current standards. Recommendations for the future standardization are given to improve the reliability and security of bus differential protection using process bus technology.

articleTitle: A protection scheme independent of fault current level for active distribution system using local measurements
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The presence of inverter interfaced distributed generation units in a distribution system puts challenge to available overcurrent protection schemes as fault current level is limited to rated current. Connection status of inverter interfaced distributed generation units and modes of operation of the distribution network vary the fault current level which further complicates the protection issue. This paper proposes a protection method based on local measurements and utilizes current and voltage phasors at the relay point to calculate active and reactive power for protection decision. No communication is required to update the status of distributed generation units and/or mode of operation. Fault current contribution from different types of distributed generation units does not affect the proposed method. The method is also tested for different configurations of transformer connected to renewable sources. The method is tested using digSilent Powerfactory simulations for a test distribution system and found to be accurate.

articleTitle: Monitoring and protection of power distribution networks with IEC 61850-9-2 standard
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: In the modern power grid, communication plays a vital role in making the system more reliable and secure. The communications network transfers data between different units to a control center or to Intelligent Electric Devices (IEDs) in order to accurately control or protect the modern power system. The paper discussed possible ways to monitor the measured values for protecting the power system according to IEC 61850-9-2 (sample value). The sequence of the process consists of streaming the sample value packet, decoding it, and phasor extraction and filtering, which are discussed here. To validate the research, Sundom Smart Grid was used as a pilot to measure the values converted to digital form (IEC 61850-9-2) and to stream it to the system through a highly secure communications network. To decode the SV packet, two scenarios are presented in the case study, based on processing useful features of the IEC 61850-9-2 standard-based raw data streamed from the SSG, including μPMU in a range of embedded instruments and a real-time simulator. The main result of this paper is an algorithm for analyzing SV packets and determining whether the network is operating normally.

articleTitle: Implementation and test of a load desensitisation algorithm in distance protection
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This article describes an approach based on sequence components which allows the necessary sensitivity to High Impedance Faults (HIF) and avoids disruptive tripping under any high load conditions. A Load Desensitisation Algorithm (LDA) based on Sequence Components has been implemented on a commercially available distance protection. The results and findings are presented and limits are discussed.

articleTitle: Single-line-to-earth protection on noneffectively-earthed distribution systems through overvoltage- and undervoltage-based philosophies
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The effectiveness of overcurrent protection on power systems concerning single-line-to-earth (SLE) faults is strongly related to the adopted neutral-earthing philosophy. Different arrangements of neutral earthing are employed for electric distribution systems (EDSs), being the unearthed, resistance-earthed, inductance-earthed and resonant-earthed designs commonly so-called noneffectively-earthed methods. SLE-fault currents can be very low in these cases, not sensitizing overcurrent-based devices. However, the voltage on the faulted phase decreases, while the voltages on non-faulted phases increase, giving rise to undervoltage and overvoltage conditions. Hence, it is possible not to be restricted to overcurrent-based philosophies but additionally uses overvoltage- and undervoltage-based ones. In this sense, this work presents a study of both overvoltage and undervoltage protections combined as a new method for SLE-fault protection, aiming the application on noneffectively-earthed EDSs. A relay in ATPDraw is modelled to trip when an undervoltage occurs at one phase and overvoltages occur at the others. ATP-EMTP simulations are performed on a representative EDS, noneffectively-earthed through a neutral earthing resistor (NER), considering different values for the fault resistance and the NER.
