The results show that the new method is more effective than the overcurrent protection for SLE faults on noneffectively-earthed systems, tripping even when that is not able to do.

articleTitle: Significance of high quality SCL data during the entire lifecycle of a protection, automation & control system
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: IEC 61850 took an unprecedented approach in also covering the configuration of systems utilizing the standard. This led to the System Configuration description Language (SCL), described in part 6 of the standard. The quality of the SCL files is crucial, not only for the system configuration itself. The System Configuration Description (SCD) file) is the fulcrum also for testing and documentation. As much of the physical wiring is transformed into communication relationships, the SCD-file has now become the most essential part of the system documentation. But this increased importance of the SCD file has long been underestimated. One reason is that the contents of the SCL files could be only reasonably assessed by the few specialists doing the engineering. Even in the early stages of a project it is beneficial to track the development of the configuration data. A Substation Section with equipment assigned to the logical nodes provides the base for a graphical representation that can be understood at a glance. Having such configuration data available is key for the effortless and complete performance of all tasks building on these data. The efforts invested in earlier stages in getting a high quality SCD-file will pay-off several times later on.

articleTitle: A current-based solution for earth-fault location in resonant-earthed medium-voltage distribution systems
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to locate earth-faults in resonant-earthed distribution systems. It uses the fundamental-frequency current measurements to determine the direction of the fault current and thereby to locate the faulted section. It sets the current-angle of the faulty phase as the reference for measuring the angles of the remaining two phase-currents. These three phasor quantities are then processed to determine the direction of the fault from the measurement point. The proposed method requires an adequate resistive current from the neutral for successfully determining the faulted section. The validity of the method has been tested by PSCAD simulations for a small-scale overhead distribution system.

articleTitle: Transient earthfault detection on petersen coil earthed systems with residually connected CT's
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The paper describes the tests undertaken at GE Stafford to verify that the Transient Earth Fault Detection (TEFD) scheme, proposed for use on the trial system, functions correctly for all fault conditions. Further consideration was taken to verify the CT type and size to ensure satisfactory operation of the scheme. The document also describes the TEFD scheme operation in detail and discusses areas where additional protection functions are required to supplement the scheme.

articleTitle: Protection, automation and control system design according to IEC 61850 – Eletrobras Eletrosul'S experience on system specification description file development
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: IEC 61850 standard is renewing the way that protection, automation and control systems (PACS) are being conceived. With the great advances in communication technology through the inner core of electrical energy system substations, several issues have been presented to project engineers, defying them to learn how to deal with new concepts and technologies. Aware of the new challenges to overcome, Eletrosul, a company member of the major Latin American electrical energy group - Eletrobras, started its own PACS definition according to IEC 61850 standard. The main objective was to create a System Specification Description (SSD) file bringing together Eletrosul experience on electrical energy substations and PACS project, construction, operation and maintenance. Focusing on SSD file feasibility to work with multi-vendor IEDs (Intelligent Electronic Devices), discussions took place with several vendors to validate the proposed PACS configuration within their tools. After some updates on the SSD file, it was possible to read it on commercial programs designed to configure IEDs and/or test PACS. This approach will improve the way PACS project and configurations are conceived, reducing engineering time, human errors and costs on protection and automation system deployment.

articleTitle: Investigation of the performance of ROCOF-based LOM protection in distribution networks with virtual synchronous generators
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This paper investigates and presents the enhancement of the performance of the most-commonly utilised Loss-of-Mains (LOM) protection, Rate of Change of Frequency (ROCOF), in multi-generator power islands, which include Virtual Synchronous Generators (VSG) instead of typical Phase-Locked-Loop-(PLL) driven Inverter-Connected (IC) generation. For this purpose, the implemented generation mixes include conventional Synchronous Generation (SG), IC generation from Photovoltaic Panels (PV) and VSG-based generation. The evaluation of the ROCOF relay is based upon the latest EREC G99 settings, with genuine islanding events applied for various generation mixes and various active and reactive power imbalances at the time of the power island formation, with the aim of assessing the Non-Detection Zone (NDZ) of each operational scenario. The results included in this paper reveal that the substitution of IC generation for VSG-based generation improves the effectiveness of ROCOF protection by restoring the NDZ coherency and increasing the reliability of the method.

articleTitle: Process bus busbar protection — A stepping stone towards digital substation
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The basic building block of a digital substation is IEC 61850 process bus, or the concept of distributed I/O for protection, control and SCADA reporting. Much of the discussion around digital substation has focused on the mechanics of the devices, architectures, and technologies to publish sampled values (SVs) from merging units (MUs) to protective relays. One challenge that has been ignored is the processing of a large amount of data streams for busbar protection. A busbar protection for a reasonably sized transmission substation requires current measurements from multiple bays, bus couplers, and other sources, which requires much more SV data streams than any other situation in the substation domain. Despite the challenge, busbar protection using process bus is simply the proven concept of a distributed busbar protection system, using MUs and SVs as opposed to dedicated bay units and proprietary communications. However, a process bus busbar protection is more than just busbar protection with SVs. It is a novel and complete solution which eliminates conventional busbar protection constraints on the bays' connections, simplifies testing, enhances protection and communications reliability and stability, and facilitates time synchronization without relying on satellite clocks. Integrating process bus simplifies the practical challenges in busbar protection. Redundant protection by connecting a second relay to the network, effortless bay and zone expansion, and reducing limitations on the number of bays and zones. Importantly, a process bus busbar protection application is not limited to just digital substation projects. It can be a standalone busbar protection system, perfect to retrofit conventional busbar protection systems and substations. Once installed, thanks to the standard process bus communication framework architecture, it becomes an excellent stepping stone to convert a conventional substation to a full digital substation.

articleTitle: Evaluation of process bus data latency with PRP/HSR enabled Ethernet switches
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Understanding the switching behaviours of Ethernet switches is critically important for analysing the transfer time of time-critical messages, e.g. Sampled Value (SV) and Generic Object Oriented Substation Event (GOOSE) messages in a complex IEC 61850 Ethernet network. Most analytical models and simulation programs estimate the network latency by assuming a symmetrical port speed at ingress and egress ports with fixed switching delays. However, the switching characteristics are product-specific and can vary significantly depending on the types of switching hardware, transferred messages and port speed. This paper evaluates the switching characteristics of PRP/HSR enabled switches by analysing the time required to forward SV, GOOSE and IEEE 1588 messages using various port types and speeds combinations. The obtained switching behaviours provide an insight into the multi-protocol traffic interactions at substation process bus. The results can also be used as a performance reference for power engineers and academic researchers to improve the accuracy of analytical models and simulation platforms.

articleTitle: Impact of voltage source converter (VSC) based HVDC interconnection on AC power system energy transmission wide-area disturbances
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The future of Power systems include high penetration of renewable energy and interconnectivity between different networks through VSC-HVDC. However, this has increased the stress on transmission systems. WAMS and WAP aim at providing an awareness of the system state and increase the robustness when faced with disturbances, thus increasing security of operation. In this context, the present work provides an overview of the key concepts and challenges of wide-area in Power System energy transmission, as well as highlighting possible impact of VSC-HVDC towards disturbances. In order to be able to assess these disturbances, this paper proposes a methodology to study of VSC-HVDC contribution towards wide-area disturbances and impact on protection systems.

articleTitle: Human aspects related to IEC 61850 testing: How to believe or don't believe in testing
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Since beginning of electricity, testing of electrical devices were done utilizing a small replica of the main network components. As it is impossible to visualize the physical phenomena (electrons circulating), in the mind of those old engineers it was create a belief of the phenomena by manipulating rheostats and dials and visualizing the movement of needles in the instrumentation. As technology evolves, and relays and other instruments become digital, but still electrical in sensing; it appears more sophisticated test equipment, where the internal process start visualizing a screen where engineers write numbers. Inside the test machine, the value written is digitalized, converted to electrical signals and sent to the device, but again, engineer cannot see all process and he believes that what is happening in the test machine and in the device under test is true. IEC 61850 [1] is being implemented in areas before dominated exclusively by electricity. With new devices, where the communication aspects become crucial, testing procedure approaches more and more with the one used to test software than hardware. Paper describes testing procedures evolution and how we forecast that it will be done in future, analysing the impact in process, minds and believes.

articleTitle: Functional testing of digital substations with optical instrument transformers
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: A Fault Induced Delayed Voltage Recovery (FIDVR), is the phenomenon whereby the system voltage remains at significantly reduced levels for several seconds after a transmission, subtransmission, or distribution fault has been cleared. The first part of the paper describes the reasons for FIDVR – large numbers of induction motors that stall due to the voltage drop during a short circuit fault at different voltage levels. The second part of the paper describes some of the methods for dealing with FIDVR and the challenges in selecting of the action to be taken: To trip the feeders with induction motors in order to speed-up the voltage recovery or To prevent the tripping of healthy feeders due to the increased current drawn by the induction motors. The last part of the paper describes how IEC 61850 can be used to help with FIDVR by implementing protection schemes resulting in faster fault clearing times or implementing adaptive schemes to optimize the decision for tripping or blocking the tripping of feeders with induction motors.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of fault detection and classification techniques for HVDC grids protection
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Dealing with high short-circuit currents with a fast rise rate in Voltage Source Converters (VSCs) still poses as a challenge for High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) multiterminal system (MTDC) reliability. Several fault detection algorithms have been proposed for multiterminal VSC-HVDC grids, such as undervoltage, overcurrent and their respective time derivatives. This work investigates their performance in terms of speed, sensitivity and correctness concerning classification. Tests were conducted by simulating pole-to-pole and pole-to-ground faults in different locations and fault resistances in a four-terminal VSC-HVDC grid. The results confirmed that voltage-based algorithms performed better than current-based algorithms in most cases. Furthermore, a voltage ratio method is proposed to increase fault classification performance during low-resistance faults.

articleTitle: Validation of dynamic GB transmission system models with PMU data for hardware-in-the-loop studies
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Decarbonisation of the electrical power system in Great Britain (GB) has impacted the dynamic behaviour of the power system, not least due to the reduction in system inertia. Following disturbance events on the power system, Fast Frequency Phenomena (F2P) can be observed which may cause mal-operation of Loss-of-Mains (LoM) protection relays on distributed generation where the relays use Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF) or Vector Shift (VS) to detect loss of mains. The research presented in this paper aims to validate a full model of the GB transmission system using Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) data from system events. The model is implemented in the DIgSILENT PowerFactory analysis software. Three types of F2P are compared in the period following the disturbance when LoM protection may be affected: simulation of electromagnetic (VS) phenomena shows some differences to actual PMU measurements, but the electromechanical and mechanical phenomena (affecting RoCoF) are in good agreement. The distribution of inter-area oscillation frequency modes following the disturbances are also closely represented in the model. Based on these studies, it can be concluded that the model is suitable for F2P studies using Hardware-in-the-Loop simulation with real LoM protection relays.

articleTitle: Algorithm for determining the inception time of earth faults in resonant earthed neutral systems
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Resonant earthed neutral is applied in most distribution systems in Central European countries. For systems with such neutral point treatment, determining the direction of earth faults is challenging for protection systems. Transient methods determine the direction of earth faults based on the transient phenomena after the inception of earth faults. Therefore, it is essential to know the exact inception time of earth faults. This paper proposes a new algorithm for determining the inception time of earth faults in resonant earthed neutral systems called DEFIT (Determination of Earth Fault Inception Time). First, an analysis of transient events, which serves as a basis for the development of the DEFIT algorithm, is shown in this paper. The DEFIT algorithm is then presented and explained in detail. It was tested with a catalogue of records from Siemens and showed promising results. This paper contributes to a better understanding of the challenge to determine the exact inception time of earth faults in resonant earthed neutral systems by comprehensively analysing transient events in the zero sequence voltage. The proposed DEFIT algorithm offers a new approach for meeting this challenge and for further improving the reliable functionality of transient earth fault relays.

articleTitle: Load blinding stabilisation of rough balance busbar protection relays
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Distribution Network Operators (DNO) face the challenge of increasing load demand on networks with low fault levels. This challenge is present at substations if the busbar protection scheme uses the overcurrent principle. The challenge is even more pronounced if that protection is to provide circuit breaker fail protection for feeder faults because fault levels at the end of the feeder can be lower than the busbar load. Both installation of additional circuit breakers for redundancy and additional busbar sections for load sharing are expensive solutions for this challenge. Circuit breaker fail back-tripping schemes on feeders pose an operational risk of customer interruption. UK Power Networks (UKPN) already use load blinding to stabilise directional overcurrent protection (DOC) on transformer incomers to enable increased distributed generation on the network. This allows the distribution transformers to export more current than DOC would see for a fault on the network. Following system studies, bench testing and site testing, UKPN is now using load blinding at applicable sites to stabilise overcurrent busbar protection so that the protection settings can be set below load levels. The function can be enabled in approved protection relays therefore the overall savings are very high.

articleTitle: On evaluating a time-domain distance element of a real relay for double-circuit transmission line protection
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This paper presents an evaluation for a time-domain distance element, presented in a commercially available relay, for double-circuit transmission line protection. Although it is widely known that traditional phasor-based distance elements are significantly affected by the zero-sequence coupling present in double-circuit transmission lines, the amount of influence in the time-domain element still unknown. As a result, the analysis presented in this paper propose to clarify the effect of zero-sequence coupling on time-domain elements. The evaluation was carried out by testing three different scenarios of network equivalent, since it affects the zero-sequence coupling since it governs the current flowing on the healthy circuit. Within each scenario, a variation of fault distance in 1% increments is performed, resulting in a total of 297 events. Overall, the time-domain distance element has demonstrated less influence on underreach and similar in overreach when compared to the traditional distance element, besides being more consistent and faster. However, special considerations are necessary to guarantee secure operation.

articleTitle: Integration of new customer tertiary connections to existing transformer protection and control arrangements and associated new solutions
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The Government has set a target for the UK to be a net zero carbon society by 2050. This is a massive National challenge, and the Electricity sector will have a major role in helping to deliver this ambition. A lot of the new connecting capacity will be smaller dispersed modules, typically below 50MW. These will include renewable generation, demand (electric vehicle charging, space heating) and grid balancing solutions. The provision of fast, secure network access for these new services is the best way for the Electricity networks to meet this demand. National Grid Electricity Transmission (NGET) has developed a new bay solution which utilises the existing 13kV tertiary winding on its Super-Grid Transformers (SGT) via a step-up transformer to provide a supply connection at 33kV. The paper introduces this new design and the challenges which must be overcome to deliver the application. The focus will be on the protection and control for the new transformer tertiary connection arrangement, highlighting the interfacing challenges with the existing protection and control systems. It also explores the considerations for the longer-term asset management and future applications associated with this type of connection.

articleTitle: Trial projects of low power instrument transformers in Harsh Scottish environments
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: Deployment of non-conventional instrument transformers in utilities is always perceived as a risk primarily due to lack of familiarity and practical exposure. SSEN pilot projects on the live network are being proposed to overcome this challenge. These pilot trials required careful selection of non-critical functions to the overall project but at the same time aims to deliver maximum learning outcomes. This paper describes the processes involved in specifying innovative applications in critical tight time scaled live project selection and market research for available products to meet the specific application and practices in place. This is further enhanced by investigating performance and reliability of associated merging units and Ethernet switches in harsh Scottish environments by installing in the switchyard as opposed to customised temperature-controlled relay rooms. A “Double-skinned” Marshalling Kiosk (MK) design shall be implemented for the outdoor installation to meet the requirements of the electronic components. The knowledge gained from the development of this design shall be utilised in the specification of future outdoor installations. SSEN's R&D and Training facility at Braco has been used to gain hands-on experience with experts from the equipment vendors and field operational engineers.

articleTitle: Design and evaluation of a single-phase directional overcurrent protection relay implemented using a raspberry PI
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The design of a directional comparison protection scheme based on the raspberry PI computer is presented in this paper. A prototype directional overcurrent relay was built, and its performance was tested. This prototype could be used as the basis for a simple, more economical protection scheme for future HV and LV networks without compromising the fault clearance requirements of a power system.

articleTitle: Challenges and solutions for fault induced delayed voltage recovery (FIDVR)
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)

articleTitle: Hardware-in-the-loop testing of line differential protection relay based on IEC 61850 process bus
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The term digital substation refers to the process of managing operations between intelligent primary devices and distributed Intelligent Electric Devices (IEDs) interfaced with a highly secure communications network. The process bus is the first part of the interface between the primary instruments (such as the current and voltage transformers and protection devices) and is an important part of digitalization. This paper describes a method for constructing an interface between measurement instruments and protection devices based on the IEC 61850 standard. Two scenarios are considered to examine the performance of the power system protection in a transmission line between two substations. Both a conventional and an IEC 61850-9-2 (sampled values) approach are implemented to feed the measured values to the protection devices. Trip signals are then also sent to the circuit breakers using IEC 61850-8-1 (GOOSE message). Comparing this method with conventional technology, the outcomes for the digital substation are more accurate and reliable thanks to the rapid reaction of protection devices and the speed at which the trip signal is received. The new process bus method has been tested by implementing a hardware-in-the-loop platform, consisting of a real-time simulator (OPAL-RT eMEGAsim), StandAlone Merging Units (SAMUs), and line differential protection.

articleTitle: Automated testing application for a novel playback functionality on a real time-domain relay
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: This paper presents an application, developed in Python, that releases the potential for extensive testing capabilities on a real time-domain relay. Such development is relevant since most of the commercially available testing equipment cannot reproduce the required fidelity for traveling wave testing. The proposed application automates the original procedure offered by the relay's manufacture, as the amount of required user inputs turns the original application time-consuming and prone to errors whether multiple test scenarios are involved. Additionally, the developed application advantage is demonstrated in terms of time reduction over the original method and by presenting a sample analysis in order to illustrate what could be achieved with the proposed tool in terms of relay evaluation.

articleTitle: Coordination of AC protection settings during energisation of AC grid from a VSC HVDC interconnector
publicationTitle: 15th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2020)
abstract: The Relatively low short circuit current limit of VSC converters in comparison to conventional synchronous generation can affect grid short circuit and dynamic characteristics during a black start. This can impair protection performance at both transmission and distribution levels. This paper investigates the protection issues related to black start and system restoration using VSC HVDC as the black start resource. A case study on the Scottish transmission system is used to examine the implications for protection devices operating in the unique scenario where the network is restored from HVDC. Given the greater flexibility in its black start operation, both traditional step by step energisation and soft energisation from the VSC HVDC are examined finding that soft energisation can mitigate the potential for large transformer inrush currents exciting resonances on the network.
